title: Add onboarding playlist for RAG sessions with minisketch tool adapters and inline eval hooks
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: provide a compact, opinionated onboarding playlist for teams adopting RAG workflows and Redwood tooling. This PR adds a guided step sequence (playlists) that walks new users through: 1) local index creation, 2) minimal tool-binding with a tiny adapter scaffold (minisketch), 3) progressive checks (inline eval hooks) that assert quality and telemetry checkpoints, and 4) smoke e2e for CI. The playlist is intentionally small so it can be executed in <15 minutes on a developer laptop. Checklist: - [x] Add playlist YAML and example corpus - [x] Add minisketch adapter templates (TS + Python) - [x] Add devcontainer with seed data for local dev - [x] Add inline eval hook examples and example assertions - [x] Add minimal e2e smoke test and CI job - [x] Update docs site quickstarts page with step-by-step run instructions Usage summary: the new quickstart can be run via scripts/quickstart-run.sh which performs: bootstrap (creates local index), start local RAG shim, run the playlist runner which executes tool-calls and inline assertions, and produce a session report under ./build/playlists/session-<id>. The minisketch adapter is a deliberately small adapter that demonstrates the shape of a tool-binding: auth shim, request/response contract, retry policy, and a telemetry probe hook. Inline eval hooks are JSONPath-style checks that run against model responses to catch regressions early and emit structured events to telemetry. Backwards compatibility: playlists are additive and live under quickstarts/onboarding-playlist; existing quickstarts are untouched. Documentation: the docs site is updated at docs/site/content/quickstarts/onboarding-playlist.md with screenshots, expected output, and troubleshooting notes. CI: added playlist-smoke workflow which runs the smoke e2e on a lightweight runner; e2e uses seeded small index to keep run time < 90s. Related work: builds on ENG-1972 (playlists infra) and PM-322 (onboarding flow design).
